title: Targeting the IKKalpha/NF-kappaB Axis with SGEC-Derived Exosomal miR-23b-3p Rebalances Treg/Th17 Immunity in Sjogren's Syndrome.
authors: Cai, Yan; Wang, Xianzhen; Feng, Jing; E, Changyong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究SGEC外泌体miR-23b-3p调控IKKalpha/NF-kappaB通路改善干燥综合征，核心为miRNA-蛋白信号通路与免疫调节，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sjogren's syndrome (SS) is a systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, and progressive salivary gland dysfunction. Current therapies remain limited in efficacy. AIM: This study explored the regulatory effect of exosome (Exo)-transported miR-23b-3p on the IkappaB kinase alpha (IKKalpha)/nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-kappaB) signaling axis in SS. METHODS: Key SS-related microRNAs (miRNAs) were identified by integrating weighted gene co-expression network analysis with machine-learning-based transcriptomic profiling. Target genes and functional pathways were analyzed by bioinformatics methods. The direct binding between miR-23b and IKKalpha (CHUK) was validated by a dual-luciferase reporter assay. An in vitro SS cell model was established to examine the effects of miR-23b-3p on the IKKalpha/NF-kappaB pathway, oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. miR-23b-3p was loaded into salivary gland epithelial cell-derived Exos (SGEC-Exos) via electroporation. In vitro coculture experiments assessed reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, inflammatory cytokines, Treg/Th17 balance, and cell apoptosis. In vivo effects were evaluated in NOD/Ltj mice by measuring salivary flow rate, histopathology, and expression of salivary-function-related proteins AQP5 and GPER. RESULTS: SGEC-Exos@miR-23b-3p significantly suppressed IKKalpha expression and NF-kappaB activation, reduced ROS production, and modulated immune responses by restoring the Treg/Th17 balance. It also inhibited apoptosis by decreasing Bax and caspase-3 expression and increasing Bcl-2 levels. These effects were partially reversed by reactivation of the IKKalpha/NF-kappaB pathway. In NOD/Ltj mice, SGEC-Exos@miR-23b-3p improved salivary flow, alleviated glandular pathology, and upregulated AQP5 and GPER expression. CONCLUSIONS: SGEC-Exos@miR-23b-3p offers a translational approach to address oxidative stress, immune imbalance, and glandular injury in SS, highlighting the potential of Exo-based miRNA therapy. Antioxid. Redox Signal. 45, 376-396.
abstract_zh: 背景：干燥综合征（Sjogren's syndrome, SS）是一种系统性自身免疫性疾病，其特征为慢性炎症、氧化应激和进行性唾液腺功能障碍。当前疗法的疗效仍有限。目的：本研究探讨了外泌体（Exo）转运的miR-23b-3p对SS中IkappaB激酶α（IKKalpha）/核因子κB（NF-kappaB）信号轴的调控作用。方法：通过整合加权基因共表达网络分析与基于机器学习的转录组谱分析，鉴定了关键的SS相关微小RNA（miRNAs）。利用生物信息学方法分析了靶基因和功能通路。通过双荧光素酶报告基因实验验证了miR-23b与IKKalpha（CHUK）之间的直接结合。建立了体外SS细胞模型，以检测miR-23b-3p对IKKalpha/NF-kappaB通路、氧化应激、炎症和凋亡的影响。通过电穿孔将miR-23b-3p装载到唾液腺上皮细胞来源的外泌体（SGEC-Exos）中。体外共培养实验评估了活性氧（ROS）水平、炎症细胞因子、Treg/Th17平衡和细胞凋亡。在NOD/Ltj小鼠中评估了体内效应，通过测量唾液流率、组织病理学以及唾液功能相关蛋白AQP5和GPER的表达。结果：SGEC-Exos@miR-23b-3p显著抑制了IKKalpha表达和NF-kappaB激活，减少了ROS产生，并通过恢复Treg/Th17平衡调节了免疫反应。它还通过降低Bax和caspase-3表达及增加Bcl-2水平抑制了凋亡。这些效应部分被IKKalpha/NF-kappaB通路的再激活所逆转。在NOD/Ltj小鼠中，SGEC-Exos@miR-23b-3p改善了唾液流率，减轻了腺体病理，并上调了AQP5和GPER表达。结论：SGEC-Exos@miR-23b-3p提供了一种转化方法，以应对SS中的氧化应激、免疫失衡和腺体损伤，突显了基于Exo的miRNA疗法的潜力。抗氧化与氧化还原信号 45, 376-396.
